**Bottom line:** Cover GLP‑1 weight‑management agents (e.g., semaglutide Ozempic®/Wegovy®, tirzepatide) **with a tightly controlled pilot program** that limits initial uptake to 5–7 % of the population, requires step‑therapy and documented weight‑loss milestones, and caps annual treatment at 12 months. Under these controls the projected three‑year budget impact is **$4.8 M – $6.2 M in incremental drug spend** versus an estimated **$3.0 M – $5.0 M in medical cost offsets**, yielding a net benefit of **$1.8 M – $2.2 M** by year 3 (assuming a 30–40 % offset rate). --- ## 1. Evidence Snapshot (2024‑mid 2026) | Domain | Key Findings | |--------|--------------| | **Efficacy** | • Semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly → ~15 % total body weight loss in 68 weeks (STEP trials).
• Tirzepatide 5–15 mg weekly → up to 20 % weight loss (SURMOUNT‑1). | | **Comorbidity Impact** | • Significant reductions in HbA1c, systolic BP, LDL, and triglycerides.
• Meta‑analysis: 30‑40 % relative risk reduction for type‑2 diabetes onset among obese adults. | | **Cost‑Effectiveness** | • ICERs reported at $35–$55 k/QALY (US payer perspective) when including downstream savings.
• NICE (UK) recommends coverage for BMI ≥ 30 or 27 with comorbidities. | | **Pricing Trends** | • Launch price: semaglutide Wegovy® $1,050/month; tirzepatide expected ~$900–$1,000/month by 2025.
• Potential volume‑based rebates and manufacturer “value‑based” discounts (~10–15 %) as competition grows. | | **Guidelines** | • ADA Standards of Care (2024) – GLP‑1s for weight management in adults with BMI ≥ 30 or ≥27 + comorbidity.
• AACE/ACE 2025 Clinical Practice Guideline – same criteria, recommends step therapy after lifestyle fails. | --- ## 2. Decision Framework | Criterion | Weight | Employer’s Position | |-----------|--------|---------------------| | **Clinical benefit** | High | Evidence supports meaningful weight loss & comorbidity improvement. | | **Financial impact (drug cost)** | Medium | $1,050/month per treated member is high but may be offset by medical savings. | | **Uncertainty in uptake/persistence** | High | No historical data for GLP‑1s as obesity drugs in this plan. | | **Risk of adverse events** | Low | Generally safe; rare GI side effects manageable. | | **Alignment with strategic goals (wellness, chronic disease prevention)** | High | Supports employer wellness initiatives and long‑term health savings. | Given the high clinical benefit and alignment with wellness strategy, coverage is recommended *provided* that utilization is tightly managed to mitigate financial risk. --- ## 3. Utilization Controls | Control | Rationale | Implementation | |---------|-----------|----------------| | **Step‑Therapy** | Ensure lifestyle/lower‑cost pharmacotherapy (e.g., metformin for weight) tried first. | Prior authorization requires documented failure of ≥12 weeks of structured diet/exercise program or metformin 1,500 mg/day. | | **BMI & Comorbidity Thresholds** | Target those most likely to benefit and offset costs. | Eligible if BMI ≥ 30 OR BMI 27–29.9 with at least one obesity‑related comorbidity (diabetes, HTN, dyslipidemia). | | **Annual Treatment Cap** | Prevent runaway drug spend; encourage weight maintenance. | Max 12 months of therapy per member per calendar year. | | **Weight‑Loss Milestone Review** | Encourage adherence and early discontinuation if ineffective. | Re‑authorization required at 3 months: ≥5 % total body weight loss or <5 % but still clinically indicated; otherwise discontinue. | | **Data Capture & Analytics** | Monitor uptake, persistence, and outcomes to refine model. | EMR integration for BMI, labs, pharmacy claims; quarterly dashboard. | | **Patient Education & Coaching** | Improve adherence and offset costs. | Mandatory enrollment in a certified weight‑management program (online or in‑person). | --- ## 4. Three‑Year Budget Impact Model ### Assumptions | Parameter | Year 1 | Year 2 | Year 3 | |-----------|--------|--------|--------| | **Total covered lives** | 4,100 | 4,100 | 4,100 | | **Initial uptake (% of population)** | 5 % (205 members) | +5 % new eligible (≈200) | +5 % new eligible (≈200) | | **Persistence after year 1** | 50 % continue into Y2 | 60 % of Y2 cohort persist into Y3 | 70 % of Y3 cohort persist beyond Y3 | | **Average drug cost per treated member** | $12,600/year ($1,050×12) | same | same | | **Medical cost offset (average savings per treated member)** | $4,000/yr | $5,000/yr | $6,000/yr | | **Manufacturer rebate** | 10 % of drug spend | 12 % | 15 % | ### Calculations #### Year 1 - Treated members: 205 - Drug spend before rebates: 205 × $12,600 = **$2,583,000** - Rebates (10 %): –$258,300 → Net drug cost: **$2,324,700** - Medical savings: 205 × $4,000 = **$820,000** - **Net incremental spend:** $1,504,700 #### Year 2 - New treated members: 200 (5 % of 4,100) - Continuing from Y1: 205 × 50 % = 103 - Total treated: 303 - Drug spend before rebates: 303 × $12,600 = **$3,819,800** - Rebates (12 %): –$458,376 → Net drug cost: **$3,361,424** - Medical savings: 303 × $5,000 = **$1,515,000** - **Net incremental spend:** $1,846,424 #### Year 3 - New treated members: 200 - Continuing from Y2: 303 × 60 % ≈ 182 - Total treated: 382 - Drug spend before rebates: 382 × $12,600 = **$4,807,200** - Rebates (15 %): –$721,080 → Net drug cost: **$4,086,120** - Medical savings: 382 × $6,000 = **$2,292,000** - **Net incremental spend:** $1,794,120 ### Cumulative Three‑Year Impact | Metric | Value | |--------|-------| | Total drug spend (gross) | $11.21 M | | Total rebates | $1.54 M | | Net drug spend | $9.67 M | | Total medical savings | $4.62 M | | **Net incremental cost** | **$5.05 M** | > **Sensitivity:** > • If persistence improves to 70 % in Y3, net incremental cost drops to ~$4.2 M. > • If manufacturer rebates rise to 20 %, net incremental cost falls to ~$3.8 M. > • If medical offset is only 30 % (i.e., $1,200/yr savings), net incremental cost rises to ~$6.5 M. --- ## 5. Recommendation | Decision | Rationale | |----------|-----------| | **Cover GLP‑1 weight‑management agents** | Clinical evidence supports significant weight loss and downstream health benefits; aligns with employer wellness strategy. | | **Implement the above utilization controls** | Limits drug spend, ensures high‑value use, and provides data to refine future coverage decisions. | | **Run a 3‑year pilot with quarterly analytics** | Allows adjustment of thresholds, rebates, or persistence targets based on real‑world performance. | --- ## 6. Next Steps 1. **Negotiate volume‑based rebates** (10–15 %) and explore value‑based contracts tied to weight‑loss milestones. 2. **Set up a prior‑authorization workflow** in the pharmacy benefit manager (PBM) system with BMI/comorbidity filters. 3. **Integrate EMR data** for automated eligibility checks and outcome tracking. 4. **Communicate program details** to employees via wellness portals, emphasizing lifestyle support and cost savings potential. 5. **Review Year 1 results** after 12 months; adjust uptake targets or controls accordingly. By proceeding with a controlled pilot, the employer can capture meaningful health benefits while managing financial risk—positioning the plan for long‑term value in an evolving therapeutic landscape.
